nan-payload.summary: Only NaN words differ: a NaN that the arithmetic makes is CUDA's canonical 0x7FFFFFFF but Metal's 0x7FC00000. The numbers are the same.
nan-payload.evidence: The arrays after the first launch that parts were saved on both machines from identical inputs (WOOF_LAUNCH_SAVE_BEFORE/WOOF_LAUNCH_SAVE). Every differing word was a NaN on both sides: noah_column 11 words, shinhong_column 1464, sfclay_classic_atanf_probe 4093, wsm6r_column 14, the topo-wind chain's shinhong_column 853. Every case was 0x7FC00000 (Metal) against 0x7FFFFFFF (CUDA).
nan-payload.closes_when: the Metal translation canonicalises the NaN an operation produces to CUDA's 0x7FFFFFFF

vendor-tgamma.summary: nssl2_fill_velocity_gamma calls binary64 tgamma. On Metal that is the vendored Rust-libm transcription (woof/backend/translate/vendor_libm64.cuh); on CUDA it is libdevice. 12 of the table's 240 words differ by 1 ULP.
vendor-tgamma.evidence: With the table as the only differing input, nssl2_sediment_all_parallel_64 on Metal gives CUDA's words (tools/kernel_probe.py replay, PR #148), and the production step matches WRF on both backends. The first-step case receives the same cached table.
vendor-tgamma.closes_when: a transcription of libdevice's tgamma replaces the vendored one

pointer-table.summary: ucm_column_test takes three uint64 tables of device addresses (its inputs, outputs and state), so their words are each process's own pointers. The outputs written through them are not launch arguments and are not digested.
pointer-table.evidence: With the launch's arrays saved on both machines, only the three address tables (17, 19 and 43 words) differ. The test compares every output word with WRF 4.6.1 and passes on both backends.
pointer-table.closes_when: never on this comparison: an address is not a computed word

cuda-only-test.summary: The test checks NVRTC's compiler identity, so it skips on the MLX backend, which has no NVRTC.
cuda-only-test.evidence: junit: passed on CUDA, skipped on MLX.
cuda-only-test.closes_when: never: the subject is CUDA's compiler

projection-libm.summary: The Lambert projection (woof.static.lambert) runs on the host through the platform's C library (woof.core.host_libm), which is macOS's libm on the Mac and glibc on pb. Every field of every portable grid differs, and the projection's words feed the kernels' map factors, Coriolis and rotation.
projection-libm.evidence: The grids of tests/fixtures/portable_static_grids.json (nests applied, as in tests/test_static_projection_portability.py), in binary64: 253,227 of 437,808 words differ. The median difference is 2 ULP, 99 % are within 6 ULP, and the largest is 52,382 ULP (rotation_m near zero). The projection tests pass on both machines because each compares with its own libm.
projection-libm.closes_when: both hosts carry the opt-in glibc 2.39 transcription (`pixi run build-native-glibc239`; tests/test_host_libm.py), which is off by default because it is LGPL

independent-powf.summary: Under GPUWM_WRF_EXACT=1, Metal's strict float32 power is WOOF's correctly rounded powf (woof/backend/translate/strict_powf.cuh), and CUDA's is CuPy's powf, which is not correctly rounded. The NSSL-2 oracle ran WRF on the CUDA adapter's Exner function (in_exner), so the step on Metal starts from 273 different Exner words of 4800 and leaves WRF in about 200 output words. The test marks this as an expected failure.
independent-powf.evidence: Against strict CuPy on an RTX A6000, CuPy's powf differs from the correctly rounded word at 343,898 of the 8,388,608 binary32 x in [0.5, 1) at y = 287/1004.5, at 404,644 of 8,388,608 random pairs, and at 0 of 234 special-value pairs. WOOF's powf on Metal differs from correct rounding at 0 of all of them (tools/strict_powf/reference.py).
independent-powf.closes_when: the opt-in WOOF_STRICT_POWF=cuda is set (a source checkout only; NOTICE). The mlx-cuda-powf receipt measures it: each of these tests passes as on CUDA.

mlx-only-test.summary: The test checks that exact binary32 midpoints of pow round to even. Only WOOF's correctly rounded powf promises that, so the test skips on CUDA and with the opt-in.
mlx-only-test.evidence: junit: skipped on CUDA, passed on MLX.
mlx-only-test.closes_when: never: the subject is the correctly rounded powf
